A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SkeletonDiffusion and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Inspection of all 28 pages in each version supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original motion-prediction experiments on AMASS, FreeMan, 3DPW, and Human3.6M, including ablations and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds training-objective ablations in Table 8 and Appendix E.4.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the linear scheduler gamma_t = 1 - t/T with a cosine scheduler described as opposite to alpha_t. Eq. (8) also changes the squared norm to an unsquared norm. These revise the stated formulation; the architecture and motion-space selection among k = 50 samples are retained. Actual implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is unchanged: AMASS, FreeMan, Human3.6M, zero-shot 3DPW, synthetic-noise evaluation, and five-second autoregressive prediction all appear in both versions. The new ablations use existing AMASS coverage.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds two internal comparators against full SkeletonDiffusion: an unrelaxed k = 1 variant and a k = 50 latent-argmin variant. External benchmark comparator sets are unchanged; DivSampling becoming DivSamp in Table 3 is only a rename.

E3.justification: The new Appendix E.4 experiments introduce controlled training configurations varying sample count and the space used to select the backpropagated sample. Section 4.1 also revises the reported noise schedule. Existing dataset splits, evaluation metrics, and prediction horizons remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 8 and Appendix E.4 add a focused ablation testing the effects of best-of-k training and motion-space versus latent-space sample selection. Existing architectural, covariance, convergence, robustness, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The newly compared k values count predictions sampled during training, not independent experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds ADE/APD results of 0.489/4.984 for k = 1 and 0.476/8.497 for k = 50 latent argmin, alongside the retained full-model values of 0.480/9.456. Diffusion-training durations are also newly reported. Pre-existing benchmark and appendix result values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Removing the square from Eq. (8) changes the mathematical objective and introduces a conflict with the unchanged squared-loss derivation in Appendix A.3, particularly Eqs. (34) and (35). No new proofs are added, and the remaining appendix derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about nonisotropic diffusion, skeletal inductive bias, realistic and diverse prediction, and deficiencies in existing diversity metrics. The added ablation supports an existing design claim.

C2.justification: Appendix E.4 newly interprets k-relaxation as improving coverage of future modes and suggests that early latent-space similarity can misrepresent motion similarity. It also identifies the substantial training-time cost of decoding all candidates for motion-space selection.

D1.justification: Appendix E.4 newly reports diffusion-only training times: five days for the standard method, one day for k = 1, and approximately 1.5 days for k = 50 latent selection. Appendix C's six-day overall training disclosure remains unchanged. Code-access information and existing implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and research-positioning claims are retained. The new ablation discussion reuses BeLFusion [5] to contextualize the k-relaxation/diversity relationship already attributed to prior work in Section 4.3.

P1.justification: Appendix E.4 gains a named training-objective discussion and clearer references to the existing ablation variants. Section 4.3 explicitly identifies z = e(Y) and adds an appendix pointer. These are localized expansions and wording edits within the retained document structure.

P2.justification: Table 8 expands from three to five result rows. Table 12 moves from page 23 to page 24 with a shortened caption, and nearby appendix text reflows. Some method labels are shortened. All 20 figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The added ablation and training-time comparison strengthen evidence for an existing design choice and disclose its computational cost. However, v3 introduces an unresolved conflict between Eq. (8) and the squared-loss derivation, while changing the scheduler description without explaining its relationship to the retained results. The PDFs do not establish whether these are documentation errors or procedural revisions, preventing a reliable net judgment between improved empirical transparency and reduced methodological consistency.
